settings.git.intro: Daoris's git reaches a private repository only as a git identity you set up here: an SSH key or an HTTPS sign-in that Daoris keeps apart from your own. Your own git sign-ins are used only where you choose them.
settings.git.terminal: The same set as `daoris-driver git identity` and `git default` at a terminal.
settings.git.fileProblem: Daoris's git identities do not read, so none is used until this is fixed: {{problem}}
settings.git.empty.headline: No git identities yet
settings.git.empty.body: Daoris's git reaches a private repository only as an identity you set up here.
settings.git.httpsFact: HTTPS · signed in through Git Credential Manager {{user}}
settings.git.refused: The host does not take this identity.
settings.git.testRepository: A repository on this host to read
settings.git.keyElsewhere: Add it where {{host}} takes SSH keys.
settings.git.keyGive: Give {{host}} this public key. It is not a secret; the private key stays in Daoris's own folder.
settings.git.copyFailed: The public key could not be copied.
settings.git.readOnlyOffSays: Daoris's git may try a push with {{label}} on {{host}} again. Mark it read only again if the host refuses it.
settings.git.removeSaysSsh: Remove deletes {{label}}'s key from Daoris's folder. The host keeps the public key until you take it off there.
settings.git.removeSaysHttps: Remove asks Git Credential Manager to erase {{label}}'s stored sign-in.
settings.git.removePointing: These point at it and fall to the next step:
settings.git.trustUnknown: {{host}} is not yet trusted. Compare a key it offers with the one it publishes, then trust it.
settings.git.trustChanged: {{host}}'s key changed since you trusted it. Do not trust it unless you know why.
settings.git.keyPublished: matches the key the host publishes
settings.git.keyNotPublished: NOT a key the host publishes
settings.git.keyNoneKnown: the host publishes none Daoris knows
settings.git.defaultsWhy: A git remote nothing else chooses for uses its host's default.
settings.git.ownWhy: Daoris's git hands none of your own keys, git configuration or stored sign-ins unless you choose them for a host here.
settings.git.ownSays: This lets Daoris's git use your own SSH keys, git configuration and stored sign-ins for {{host}} wherever no git identity is chosen nearer, and a session's git reaches {{host}} as you.
settings.git.whereHint: The host and a name for this identity.
settings.git.keyHint: A new ed25519 key is made in Daoris's own folder, or you import one key file.
settings.git.rsaWhy: This host takes RSA keys alone, so the new key is RSA 4096.
settings.git.importWhy: A key with a passphrase is refused: Daoris's git cannot ask for it.
settings.git.importSays: This reads one key file of yours and copies it into Daoris's own folder. Daoris reads nothing else of yours.
settings.git.signInHint: Git Credential Manager stores the sign-in; Daoris keeps nothing.
settings.git.tokenWhy: The token goes to Git Credential Manager and is not kept anywhere else.
settings.git.commitsAsHint: Optional: the name and email a commit carries where a repository names none.
settings.git.httpsAdded: {{host}}'s sign-in is stored through Git Credential Manager under Daoris's own name.
settings.git.thenTest: Then test it on the identity's row: it is saved, and a failed test leaves it with its mark.
settings.git.noPicker: This window has no file picker. Type the key file's whole path.
settings.git.remotes.why: A git remote's identity is chosen here, else by its workspace, else by its host's default.
settings.git.remotes.none: This repository has no git remote.
settings.git.remotes.local: A local path: no identity needed.
settings.git.remotes.ownTitle: Use your own git sign-ins for {{remote}}
settings.git.remotes.ownSays: This lets Daoris's git use your own SSH keys, git configuration and stored sign-ins for {{remote}}, and a session's git reaches it as you.
settings.git.workspace.title: Git
settings.git.workspace.why: The git identity each host its repositories reach uses, unless a repository's git remote says otherwise.
settings.git.workspace.none: No repository of this workspace has a git remote on a host.
settings.git.workspace.ownSays: This lets Daoris's git use your own SSH keys, git configuration and stored sign-ins for {{host}} in this workspace, and a session's git reaches it as you.
settings.git.moved.title: Daoris's git no longer uses your own git sign-ins
settings.git.moved.says: {{count}} git remotes on {{hosts}} have no git identity yet, so Daoris's git does not reach them.
settings.git.moved.own: {{count}} of them name their own authentication or ssh command.
settings.git.moved.keep: Keep using my own sign-ins for these…
settings.git.moved.keepTitle: Keep using your own git sign-ins for these hosts
settings.git.moved.keepSays: This lets Daoris's git use your own SSH keys, git configuration and stored sign-ins for {{hosts}} on this machine.
settings.git.access.title: Git access
settings.git.access.asToday: Daoris's default: the landing pushes on your yes; sessions do not push
settings.git.access.why.read: What fetching, pulling and cloning may do on a remote: allowed, asked of you at the door while the act waits, or refused.
settings.git.access.why.write: What a push may do on a remote. A value you set holds for the landing and for a session alike; an LFS upload over HTTPS goes past this door, though the push that makes its objects reachable is still judged.
settings.git.access.oneValue.label: Use one value for both…
settings.git.access.oneValue.why: Sets Read and Write to the same value at this level.
settings.git.access.oneValue.field: One value for Read and Write for {{name}}
settings.git.access.confirm.label: Loosen git access for {{name}}
settings.git.access.confirm.read: Reading a remote will no longer be refused for {{name}}.
settings.git.access.confirm.write.allow: Sessions may push to a remote without asking you for {{name}}.
settings.git.access.confirm.write.ask: Sessions may push for {{name}} when you allow each push at the door.
